title: Elements of weather and climate
competency: Describe temperature, rainfall, air pressure and wind.

keywords.def: Transfer of energy by electromagnetic waves, as the sun warms the earth.
Transfer of heat by contact between molecules; most important in solids.
Transfer of heat through gases or liquids because of differences in density.
Any moisture that falls from the clouds towards the earth's surface.
The weight of air on a unit of area of the earth's surface, measured with a barometer.
The horizontal movement of air, from high pressure to low pressure.

en.text: Temperature is the hotness or coldness of something, measured with a thermometer. The sun's energy (insolation) heats the earth. Heat moves by radiation (electromagnetic waves), conduction (contact, best in solids) and convection (flow in gases and liquids).

screens.text: Why is the handle of a clay jebena cooler than a metal pot handle on the same fire?
opts: Clay conducts heat poorly; metal conducts well
screens.ans: Clay conducts heat poorly; metal conducts well

en.text: Rainfall is liquid precipitation, measured with a rain gauge; it is part of the water cycle powered by the sun. Rain is relief, convectional or frontal. Air pressure, measured with a barometer, falls with height. Wind is air moving from high to low pressure, measured with an anemometer, named after where it comes from.

screens.ask: Why do the windward slopes of the Ethiopian highlands get more rain than the lowlands nearby?
opts: Moist air rises over the mountains, cools and rains
The lowlands are too hot for clouds
screens.after: Moist air is forced up the mountains, cools, condenses and falls as rain: relief (orographic) rainfall.

Precipitation is any moisture that falls from clouds.
It is part of the hydrological cycle, powered by solar energy.

screens.title: Air pressure and wind
paras: Air pressure is the weight of air on a unit area. It is measured with a barometer.
At sea level it is 1,013 millibars. It falls with height and with rising temperature.
Wind is the horizontal movement of air, from high to low pressure. An anemometer measures its speed; a wind vane shows its direction.
screens.note: A southerly wind comes FROM the south.
